subject: Cohort bridge credit wiring and discount appendix
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna@foundrylabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Intro — Foundry Labs cohort: vouchers + dedicated conversion question

Hi Stephanie / Ben / Lauren,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Quick follow-up from the program team: we run a three-team cohort in April and have a pool of promotional vouchers we want to apply as a partial bridge to a Reserved (Dedicated) conversion for two startups if they hit milestones. Two questions we need clarified before procurement: 1) can the vouchers be split across multiple accounts/projects and remain eligible for the conversion discount, and 2) is there a documented appendix or addendum that lists conversion discount tiers when promo credits are applied?

Attached is a short prospectus on the cohort schedule and expected spend profile — hoping to get a short proposal and mutual action plan so we can loop procurement.

Foundry is on a tight timeline (procurement review by 3/20). Can you confirm who owns the pricing decision and whether an exception path exists for cohort-split credits?

Thanks,
Anna Ruiz
Program Lead, Foundry Labs
Attachment: foundry-prospectus.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intro — Foundry Labs cohort: vouchers + dedicated conversion question

Team — forwarding Anna's note. High-level asks: split vouchers across projects and whether promo credits disqualify or change the conversion discount to Dedicated. Procurement wants a written appendix they can attach to the PO.

My read: we have standard policy that promo credits can be used toward Hosted consumption but conversion to Dedicated usually requires a minimum committed spend and discounts are applied to committed invoices (not to one-off promo credits). That said, we have precedent for a carve that treats promo vouchers as a credited deposit if the customer converts within 90 days — applied toward commit and triggering a modest conversion discount (5–10%) on the committed rate. I don't have the exact wording that procurement would accept.

Can you two propose phrasing and a conditional MAP that (a) allows splitting vouchers across projects within the same org, (b) defines the conversion window and credit application mechanics, and (c) lists discount tiers by commit size. Procurement needs something doc-ready by 3/18.

If we can get a short template and legal-friendly bullets, I'll send to Anna and loop legal only if the customer accepts the draft.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0149
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@foundrylabs.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro — Foundry Labs cohort: vouchers + dedicated conversion question

Anna — thanks for the clear summary and timeline. Below is a conditional approach we can commit to today; happy to iterate.

--- Proposal (conditional MAP) ---
1) Voucher splitting: Promo vouchers may be allocated across up to three separate projects/accounts under Foundry Labs’ org. Vouchers remain time-bound and are redeemable for Hosted consumption only.

2) Conversion creditization: If Foundry Labs elects to convert to Redwood Dedicated within 90 days of the voucher issuance date, unused voucher value may be converted to a one-time credit toward the first Dedicated invoice (applied as a prepayment). Converted voucher value will be recognized as a credit against committed spend at the time of conversion; credit does not change underlying SKU rates unless a committed contract is signed.

3) Discount appendix (tiers):
  - Commit >= $50k/month: 15% discount on committed per-token rates for 12 months
  - Commit >= $25k/month: 10% discount for 12 months
  - Commit >= $10k/month: 5% discount for 6 months

4) Edge cases / procurement language: Credits converted to Dedicated must be documented on the SOW/addendum and applied to the first invoice. Any remaining voucher balance after conversion remains eligible for Hosted consumption until expiry. We will require a single organizational invoice owner to accept the addendum.

5) Next steps and timeline:
  - Foundry to confirm allocation (which startups/projects get vouchers) by 3/14
  - Redwood provides final MAP/doc appendix by 3/17
  - Foundry procurement to issue PO by 3/20

I attached a quick MAP spreadsheet with fields for allocation and acceptance to make procurement work easier. If acceptable I can convert this into an SOW addendum and route to legal; otherwise we can keep to the MAP and sign off operationally.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx
